No actions yet. Laying out the approaches is its own step, and I'll write the design right after.

---

Understood. I'll write it up now. Since you've been talking about what the brewery needs and leaving the building to me, I'll make the build choice myself. Here are the options I weighed, so you can stop me if one looks wrong:

1. **Add it to the taproom app you already run on the Pi** (my pick). New records for batches, sack lots, which lots went into which batch, and bottling runs. A USB barcode scanner reads lot numbers when a sack is opened, so nobody types with wet hands. Labels print from the same app. It's the same code, the same database and the same machine you already keep running, so there's one thing to look after.
2. **A separate small app on the same Pi.** This keeps brewing records apart from the bar tabs. But it gives you two apps to update and two databases to back up, with nothing gained that you've asked for.
3. **Off-the-shelf brewery software** (Breww, Ekos and the like). Tracing is built in, but you pay a subscription, your records live in the cloud, and you'd lose the setup we just designed around your scanner and label printer.

I'm going with option 1. One thing I'll build into the design: these records are what you'd need for a recall, and right now everything lives on one Pi. So the design will include an automatic daily backup off the Pi.

This is a project-sized piece of work, so I'll write it as a proper design document in the repo's `specs/` folder. Before you see it, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it. I may come back to you once with a few questions from that review. After that, the document is yours to approve.
